source_summary: Ink-and-wash Chinese landscape with misty distant peaks and water at left/center, a dominant wind-bent pine growing from a rocky cliff, pale vertical cliffs at upper right, reeds and banks in the foreground, and a small pavilion with a scholar among rocks and leafy branches at lower right. Red seals, calligraphy, borders, and paper texture are excluded from motifs.

motifs.name: distant_left_misty_peaks
motifs.description: Isolate the pale distant mountain range on the left: clustered vertical peaks and low ridges emerging from mist, without nearby red seals or foreground bank details.
must_preserve: soft gray ink washes fading into the paper
irregular pointed peak silhouettes
vertical diluted wash streaks on the taller spires
mist-softened base edges
subtle layered ridgelines behind the main peaks

motifs.name: central_lake_and_low_hills
motifs.description: Isolate the middle-distance water surface with low hills and islands across the center-left, including the faint shoreline bands and misty horizontal washes.
must_preserve: horizontal ink-wash bands suggesting water
soft low hill contours
small darker island and shoal accents
blurred mist transitions between water and land
thin broken shoreline strokes

motifs.name: foreground_reed_bank
motifs.description: Isolate the lower-center foreground bank with sparse reeds, grasses, and pale water margins, avoiding the left seals and the large right rock mass.
must_preserve: fine dry-brush reed stems
scattered dark grass tips
pale sandbar and water-edge washes
curving low bank contour
delicate broken ink lines crossing the foreground

motifs.name: wind_bent_pine_on_cliff
motifs.description: Isolate the dominant pine tree growing from the central-right cliff: twisted trunk, leaning branches, radiating needle clusters, and the immediate craggy rock support.
must_preserve: starburst pine needle clusters
dark angular branch linework
twisted trunk with dense black strokes
dry-brush rock texture on the cliff face
long drooping branch and hanging needle sprays
contrast between dark pine ink and pale cliff wash

motifs.name: upper_right_misty_cliffs
motifs.description: Isolate the high pale cliffs in the upper right background, excluding the red seal and lower pavilion area; include the vertical rock faces and soft atmospheric washes.
must_preserve: tall vertical cliff silhouettes
layered gray wash planes
soft mist-softened edges
dark cap-like ink accents near the peaks
faint vertical texture strokes
small dark foliage mass along the far right edge

motifs.name: lower_right_pavilion_scholar
motifs.description: Isolate the small pavilion at lower right with its pitched roof, railings, posts, and the seated scholar figure inside, without adjacent calligraphy or seals.
must_preserve: precise roof geometry and dark roof wash
thin railing and post linework
seated scholar silhouette inside the pavilion
rectangular architectural framing
dark surrounding shrub washes that anchor the structure
small ink accents under the eaves

motifs.name: rocky_stair_path
motifs.description: Isolate the stone steps and rocky path leading toward the lower-right pavilion, including adjacent angular rocks but not the red seal or inscription on the far right.
must_preserve: stepped diagonal rhythm of the stair stones
dark angular rock outlines
layered gray washes on path edges
dry-brush texture in the foreground rocks
small black accents marking stone breaks
transition from steps into the darker rocky base

motifs.name: right_leafy_branch_screen
motifs.description: Isolate the airy branching tree and leafy screen above and beside the pavilion, with small triangular leaf clusters and thin arching branches, excluding the nearby red seal.
must_preserve: thin curving branch linework
small triangular leaf clusters
varied spacing of sparse foliage
light ink wash behind the branches
delicate twigs crossing open mist
contrast between fine leaves and darker lower shrubs

planning_prompt:
Analyze this Chinese landscape painting as a source for a motif bank.

Create exactly 8 reusable motifs. Return JSON only.

For each motif:
- Use a short snake_case name.
- Describe what should be isolated.
- Provide a normalized bbox as [x, y, width, height], where 0,0 is the top-left of the full image.
- Include all visible brushwork for that motif, but do not include unrelated neighboring motifs.
- Prefer motifs that can be recombined into a new coherent Chinese painting: mountains, hillsides, village clusters, pavilion groups, water/lotus surfaces, bridges, scholar figures, boats, clouds, rocks, shrubs, pines, willows, bamboo.
- Capture details that must be preserved: linework, wash texture, roof geometry, tree needles, rock texture, mist edges, and color accents.

Do not invent objects that are not visible in the source image.
Do not include calligraphy, seals, labels, borders, or paper texture as motifs unless explicitly requested.
